title: How many coins at the start, and what cost suits the genie?
description: Coins double each time around a banyan tree, and eight coins go to the genie. A letter for the starting coins gives eight ex take away forty eight equals eight, so seven coins. A letter for the cost then answers the other two parts.
teaching_notes: One idea: follow the coins through each round with a letter, then change the fixed cost eight into a letter see. Watch for students who forget to double the earlier payments in later rounds.

video_script.why: The child uses the double and take away working from the sticker puzzle over three rounds, then swaps the fixed payment for a letter to answer the other two parts.
video_script.substitution: Let x be the start: 2x − 8, 4x − 24, 8x − 48 = 8, x = 7. With cost c: 2x − c > x when c < x; after three rounds 8x − 7c, zero when c = 8x ÷ 7.
video_script.anchor: a banyan tree with a genie, the coins doubling each round and eight coins paid to the genie, repeated three times

final_answer.value: (i) 7 coins (ii) a cost less than the starting coins, fewer than 7 (iii) 8 ÷ 7 of the starting coins, which is 8 when the start is 7
final_answer.spoken: Laksh started with seven coins, a good deal has a cost below the starting coins, and the genie sets the cost at eight sevenths of the start

video_script.fraction_reading: eight sevenths is read as eight divided by seven

names.Laksh: the child who goes around the banyan tree

maths_rules: (i) let x be the start; after round 1: 2x − 8; after round 2: 2 (2x − 8) − 8 = 4x − 24
the third doubling gives 8x − 48, and this is 8, so 8x = 56 and x = 7
(ii) with cost c, one round turns x into 2x − c, which is more than x only when c < x
(iii) after three rounds with cost c: 8x − 7c; zero when c = 8x ÷ 7
for the start 7, c = 8 × 7 ÷ 7 = 8, and it is whole for starts that are multiples of 7
video_script.design: One idea: a letter for the starting coins follows three rounds, and a letter for the cost answers the other two parts. The tree and the rounds stay on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. Laksh meets a genie by a banyan tree.
<bookmark mark='round'/>Each time Laksh goes around the tree, the coins in the pocket double. Then eight coins are given to the genie.
<bookmark mark='third'/>On the third round, the coins double to exactly the eight coins owed.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many coins did Laksh have at the start?
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Then, what cost for each round suits Laksh, and what cost lets the genie win all the coins?

beats.on_screen: the tree and the rounds stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: doubling = times 2; paying the genie = take away; a letter x stands for the coins at the start

marks.ops: doubling is marked as times 2 and paying as take away
marks.letter: a box with the letter x stands for the coins at the start

narration: <bookmark mark='ops'/>Doubling means times two, and paying the genie means taking coins away.
<bookmark mark='letter'/>The coins at the start are not known, so a letter can stand for them.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 rounds; each round doubles the coins, then 8 are paid; after the third doubling exactly 8 are left to pay

marks.given: the three rounds and the number 8 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three rounds, each doubling the coins and then paying eight. After the third doubling, exactly eight coins are left to pay.

beats.on_screen: To find: (i) the coins at the start; (ii) a cost that suits the child; (iii) a cost that suits the genie

marks.find: the three aims are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three things. First the coins at the start. Then a cost that suits Laksh, and a cost that suits the genie.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, part (i): let x = the coins at the start; round 1: 2x − 8; round 2: 2 (2x − 8) − 8 = 4x − 24

marks.let: x is written as the coins at the start

beats.colours: each round in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='let'/>Step one, part one. Let ex be the coins at the start.
<bookmark mark='one'/>After one round, the coins are two ex take away eight.
<bookmark mark='two'/>In round two, double that and take away eight again. This leaves four ex take away twenty four.

marks.three: the third doubling 8x − 48 is written and set equal to 8
marks.add: 48 is added to both sides to give 8x = 56

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, double once more to get eight ex take away forty eight. This is exactly eight.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add forty eight to both sides, and eight ex is fifty six.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Divide fifty six by eight, and ex is seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, part (ii): cost c; one round: x → 2x − c; 2x − c is more than x only when c is less than x

marks.cost: the cost c replaces 8 and one round gives 2x − c
marks.less: c is less than x is written, with c less than 7 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='cost'/>Step three, part two. With a cost of see, one round turns ex into two ex take away see.
<bookmark mark='more'/>That is more than ex only when see is less than ex.
<bookmark mark='less'/>The coins grow only if the cost is below the coins in the pocket. Here that means a cost below seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, part (iii): after 3 rounds: 8x − 7c; the genie wants 0, so c = 8x ÷ 7

marks.rounds: 2x − c is written for round one
marks.more: 4x − 3c and 8x − 7c are written for rounds two and three

narration: <bookmark mark='rounds'/>Step four, part three. With cost see, the three rounds leave two ex take away see.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then four ex take away three see, and then eight ex take away seven see.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The genie wants all the coins, so nothing must be left. Eight ex take away seven see must be zero.
<bookmark mark='cost'/>Then seven see is eight ex, so see is eight ex divided by seven.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step five, put in the seven from part one. Eight times seven divided by seven is eight.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>This is the cost of eight in each round that the genie asked for.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step six, check with seven and a cost of eight. Seven doubled is fourteen, and fourteen take away eight is six.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Six doubled is twelve, and twelve take away eight is four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Four doubled is eight, and eight take away eight leaves nothing.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (i) 7 coins (ii) a cost less than the starting coins, here less than 7 (iii) c = 8 ÷ 7 of the starting coins, which is 8 for a start of 7

marks.ans: the answers to all three parts are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Laksh started with seven coins. A good deal has a cost below the starting coins. The genie sets the cost at eight sevenths of the start.
